note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a GER 10-12, 37, 8 in conjuction Administrative regulation 8.1.1., 8.1.2.; A06b GER 10-12, 37, 8 in conjuction Administrative regulation 8.1.1., 8.1.2.; L05 GER 25): ordinary naturalisation after 8 years' residence; the applicant must give up other citizenships (with major exceptions); a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another (with exceptions). Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. The Act to Modernise Nationality Law (in force 27 June 2024) changed all three, as the Nationality Act reads today: naturalisation after five years' lawful habitual residence (§ 10(1)); the renunciation requirement (§ 12) and the loss of German citizenship on taking another (§ 25) are repealed, so other citizenships are kept either way.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Germany, 2024
sources.said: Person is over the age of 16, has been resident in Germany for 8 years and is entitled to permanent residence (without permanent residence, naturalisation is not an entitlement, but can be acquired on a discretionary basis). ... Renunciation or automatic loss of citizenship of another country (unless this is legally impossible or unreasonable or if person is a citizen of an EU Member State or Switzerland). ... Person acquires citizenship of another country by naturalisation and does not obtain permission to retain German citizenship (discretionary). Provision does not apply if person acquires citizenship of an EU Member State or Switzerland.
